area: Focus ring, contrast theme, Orbit item (.ds-taskitem running/active/attention bar, line 227)
problem: In the contrast theme the Orbit item's bar paints over one of the two rows of the inner (-2px) focus ring. The bar is `::after`, bottom 1px, 3px high, `--color-text-muted`, which is white in the contrast theme. Pixel columns from `scratch/ring/017-019-tab.png` read: bar y54-56 #FFFFFF, ring only at y57 (#FFE34D), then black. The overlap is 12 px wide for running and active and 24 px for attention. The white bar directly touches the ring at 1.28:1. The doc's summary claims a 1 px gap between the contrast ring and white marks (DESIGN-SYSTEM.md lines 18-19, §10), and O-K2 does not record this case. The ring is intact and above 3:1 against black on the other three sides.
fix: In the contrast theme, move the bar clear of the ring, for example `[data-theme="contrast"] .ds-taskitem::after { bottom: 4px }`, giving a 1 px black gap like the tab and row rules. Alternatively, hide the bar while the item is focus-visible. Otherwise, add the case to O-K2 with its pixel extent.

area: Focus ring, contrast theme, menu trigger vs open menu (.ds-menu top: calc(100% + var(--space-1)), line 234)
problem: The open menu sits 4 px below its trigger. The trigger's outer ring takes exactly those 4 px (2 px offset plus 2 px width), so the ring touches the menu's white top edge. In `scratch/ring/030-tab.png`: button edge y41, black gap y42-43, ring y44-45, menu edge #FFFFFF at y46. The ring meets white at 1.28:1 along 89 px. The gallery ships the menu open, and the Tab walk reaches the trigger in that state. O-K2 does not record this.
fix: In the contrast theme, add at least 1 px to the menu offset, for example `[data-theme="contrast"] .ds-menu { top: calc(100% + 5px) }`. Alternatively, record the case in O-K2.

area: O-K2 (line 1128): compact place badge against the row's inner ring, contrast theme
problem: Already recorded; this check corroborates it. In the compact row clip `scratch/ring/050-tab.png`, a white badge edge sits at y12 directly under the ring (y10-11) from x310 to x434. 266 white pixels lie within 2 px of the ring; the lowest junction, the anti-aliased #E9E9E9 next to #FFE34D, is 1.06:1. O-K2 records 258 pixels at 1.06:1. The 38-pixel hits on standard rows are the ring's own anti-aliased corners. The standard row blade (x13, ring x10-11) and the tab panel (black y8 between the ring and the white line) both keep the documented 1 px gap.
fix: No new action beyond O-K2. Close it together with the two cases above, for example with one contrast-theme rule that keeps every white mark at least 1 px from an inner ring.

area: §4 (lines 286-290) and §11: --color-line edges and the privacy ask edge below 3:1
problem:
Measured from computed styles at 1440 px:
- `--color-line` edges in dark (window, menu, toast, info banner, privacy): 1.27:1 (#232A47 on #12162A).
- The same edges in light: 1.31:1 (#D8DEE9 on #FBFCFE).
- Place badge edges: 1.03:1 dark, 1.03:1 light, 1.00:1 light on hover.
- Privacy ask edge (`--place-internet-line`, 50 % alpha): 2.33 dark, 2.34 in the 200 % strip, 2.17 light.
The doc says so: §4 calls the `--color-line` edges information-only, by design judgement rather than measurement, and §11 calls the ask edge a supplementary cue under 3:1. Each component is also identified by fill, icon or text, and the ask state by the double-ring node and the sentence. These are therefore not WCAG 1.4.11 failures. However, the identification claim is not backed by measurement.
fix: Add these measured ratios to §4 and §11. For each component, record which cue identifies it, for example place badge = node shape + icon + label, measured 5.28:1 or better (pixel median). Then replace 'not a measured check' with this measured evidence. Do not raise the ask edge; it is redundant.

area: Contrast theme: translucent gradient ends (lines 154, 166-167, 212, 228) against the §13 'complete theme (opaque ...)' claim (DESIGN-SYSTEM.md line 856)
problem:
Several marks fade to `transparent` at both ends, and the contrast theme has no override for them:
- the row blade `::before`
- the privacy connectors
- the active-window blade `::before`
- the Orbit active blade `::before`
In the contrast theme the outer 15-26 % of each mark is partly transparent white over black. The solid centre carries the cue at 21:1, and the row selection also has its inset edge and weight 600, so nothing fails. However, the theme is not fully opaque as §13 states. The translucency scan (fills, borders, shadows, opacity, backdrop) cannot see gradient stops, so these were found by reading the source.
fix: Add solid contrast-theme backgrounds, for example `[data-theme="contrast"] .ds-row::before { background: var(--color-blade) }`. Alternatively, narrow the §13 wording to 'opaque surfaces and fills; decorative blades keep their faded ends'.

area: Provenance: citations of git-ignored build/ paths (§3.2 line 107, §4, §4.1, §10; icons.js header)
problem: The doc cites `build/design-evidence/...` 29 times: gen_tables.py, mapping.tsv, contrast_pairs.py, tune.py, check_tokens.py, check-report.txt, measure.json and the repair-2 evidence. The `icons.js` header cites `build/design-evidence/ds-1.0/work/gen_icons.py`. `build/` is git-ignored (.gitignore line 12). The light † derivations exist only in the ignored `build/design-evidence/ds-1.0/work/mapping.tsv`; examples are `--material-launch` light, `--elev-launcher` light and `--color-surface-surround`. §13 records only the contrast derivations. Once the doc is committed, these rationales and scripts will not exist in the repository. The check found no contradiction with v2: 130 † cells, 13 of them repair-1 rows recorded in §4.1, 117 in themes where v2 defines no value, and 0 where v2 defines a different value. O-C1 acknowledges the problem only for the D3 run.
fix: Store compact copies of mapping.tsv, gen_tables.py, contrast_pairs.py and check_tokens.py, with their reports and SHA-256 hashes, under `docs/verification/ds-1.0/`, and point the citations there. Alternatively, add a light-derivation table, mirroring the §13 contrast table, to §4.1 or §13.

problem: The doc says 'Native `showModal()` keeps Tab inside the dialog'. Measured with real Tab presses in headless Chrome: after the last dialog control, Tab moves to the document (BODY; in a headed browser this is the browser UI) and then returns into the dialog. Pattern: [false, true, true, false]. Page content behind the modal is inert and is never reached, and Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the opener. There is no keyboard trap and no leak, but the sentence overstates what happens.
fix: Reword to: '`showModal()` makes the page behind the dialog inert; Tab cycles through the dialog controls and the browser UI, never page content; Escape always closes it.'

problem: The doc says the gallery's warning banner and error empty state 'use this wording', that is, LOCAL-PRIVACY-CONTRACT §1 'visibly paused; files are not forwarded to another host'. The gallery actually uses the approved sentence from NAMING-AND-IA.md (lines 126-127) and `ui/design/prototype/strings.js` line 181: 'Thuis-NAS is niet bereikbaar. Je werk staat veilig op dit apparaat en wordt bijgewerkt zodra de NAS terug is.' That sentence implies a pause and no forwarding but does not state either.
fix: Reword to: 'the gallery's warning banner and error empty state use the NAMING-AND-IA.md sentence, which expresses this behaviour'. Alternatively, if the product needs the contract wording to be explicit, record an open item to add 'niet naar een andere plek gestuurd' to the copy.
